nodes.name: ContaGen Discover
nodes.notes: Tier 1. DiscoLike /contacts/discover in domain mode, one call per band group per 250 domains, results_by_company = the band cap. Paced 4.5 s apart (documented limit 15 req/min on the Team plan; left as is 2026-09-02, its 429s are documented and the saving would be a minute); a 429 retries up to 5 times 5 s apart instead of dying. Bills net-new only inside its 90-day cache.

@@file:nodes/SQ-Requests.js

@@file:nodes/Build-People.js

nodes.name: Any People?
nodes.notes: Fed by Build People (writer) or Build Ark People (ark): one People pipeline for both modes from here to the writer.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Apply-DNC.js
@@file:nodes/Chunk-People.js

nodes.name: Write People
nodes.notes: The one People writer, both modes (ruled 2026-09-02): PATCH /v0/{base}/{People} with {performUpsert: {fieldsToMergeOn: ["Contact Key"]}, records (ten per request), typecast: true}, 200 ms apart, so 50 rows per second against the Airtable node's measured 4.5. No retry: a 429 locks the base for 30 s; a request that is not 2xx counts every record in it as a write error with the reason and the pass continues. Written rows are counted from the answer's records[], never from item ids.

nodes.name: Writer Pass?
nodes.notes: After the writer (or with nothing to write): the writer batch goes on to stamp its companies and recount; the ark pass stamps nothing new and closes.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Stamp-Rows.js

nodes.name: Stamp Companies
nodes.notes: The one Companies writer: Contacts Pulled At = now on every company in the batch, PATCH by record id, ten per request, 200 ms apart, no retry; a request that is not 2xx counts its ten as stamp errors. Stamped rows are counted from the answer's records[].

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Recount-Filters.js

nodes.name: Recount People
nodes.notes: What the base holds now at the batch's domains, after the writer and the stamps: the batch's coverage. Domain on People is a lookup through the Companies link; the {Domain} filter matches its text, the field comes back as an array of one.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Ark-Plan.js
@@file:nodes/Ark-Requests.js

nodes.name: Ark Export
nodes.notes: Tier 3, one lane per run, fired by the parent once the writer lane drained and not awaited. AI-Ark Export People with Email (POST /v1/people/export, verified in docs 2026-09-02), one call per company still under its cap after the writer (the held state came with the item, from that batch's recount), size = the gap, held LinkedIn URLs excluded. 0.5 credits per person plus 0.5 per email found. The export's webhook is AI-Ark Export Callback's door with ?run=<parent execution id>; completion is read from the data table that door fills. Paced 250 ms apart, four per second: AI-Ark's ceiling (5 per second, 300 per minute) is global, and since 2026-09-02 nothing else in the run is talking to it. Fed fifty at a time by Ark Windows so the 429 breaker can stop the submission.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Ark-Track.js
@@file:nodes/Ark-Pending.js

nodes.name: Read Callbacks
nodes.notes: The completion webhooks AI-Ark Export Callback recorded, one local query per pending track id (a local read, no API, no credits). Data table ai_ark_callbacks (id PYw0JjF0o7FLmaPw; columns trackId string, state string, found number, total number, run string, receivedAt string, payload string), created by the Operator 2026-09-02.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Ark-Check.js
@@file:nodes/Fill-Found.js

nodes.name: Ark Statistics
nodes.notes: FREE, one read per export whose statistics the webhook did not settle: a DONE webhook without statistics.found, or no webhook inside the 4-minute cap (the safety net). GET /v1/people/export/{trackId}/statistics (verified in docs): state PENDING | DONE, statistics { total, found }. Paced 250 ms apart, four per second, under the global ceiling the lane owns alone.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Ark-Found.js
@@file:nodes/Ark-Result-Items.js

nodes.name: Ark Results
nodes.notes: GET /v1/people/export/{trackId}/inquiries?page&size (verified in docs; size max 100), paged until last, only for exports with found > 0 (78 percent return nothing, measured 2026-09-02, and are never fetched). Already paid at submission. Paced 250 ms apart, four per second, under the global ceiling the lane owns alone.

nodes.name: Log Batch
nodes.notes: This pass's own Hub row (ruled 2026-09-02), upsert on Execution ID "<parentExecId>-<batchNum>" or "<parentExecId>-ark", Client attached, Tally = the counters JSON the parent sums. Loud: a failed write crashes into the Error Logger instead of vanishing.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Batch-Response.js

nodes.name: Ark Windows
nodes.notes: Fifty exports per window (about 13 s at 250 ms apart). The window is the granularity the 429 circuit breaker works at: without it the node fires every planned export before anything can look at an answer, which is how execution 7954 burned about 1,679 rate-limited calls. Its done output means every planned export was submitted.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Ark-Window.js

nodes.name: Ark Window
nodes.notes: The window's requests, re-emitted so Ark Track and Ark Window Check can pair answers to requests run by run without touching a loop branch index.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Ark-Window-Check.js

nodes.name: Ark Window Check
nodes.notes: The circuit breaker: the trailing run of HTTP 429 answers across every window so far. Eight in a row and the lane stops submitting.

nodes.name: Keep Submitting?
nodes.notes: True means stop: eight AI-Ark answers in a row were HTTP 429, so no further export is submitted and Ark Track records the rest as unserved. False takes the next window.
